scenes.title: Paul Ekman and Wallace Friesen advancing a 16mm Steenbeck film viewer one frame at a time to catch a 2-frame brow flash
scenes.era: 1969, Langley Porter Neuropsychiatric Institute film lab, UC San Francisco

layout.description: Sunlit 1969 UCSF film-analysis room featuring a flatbed 16mm Steenbeck editing console with glowing ground-glass viewing screen, numbered frame counter ('Frame 14 -> Frame 15'), anatomical Action Unit charts pinned on the wall, and clipboards.

positions.who: Paul Ekman (mannequin in 1969 tweed blazer and open shirt)
positions.where: turning the hand-crank frame advance knob one click at a time while pointing a grease pencil at Frame 14 on the bright viewer screen

positions.who: Wallace Friesen (mannequin in 1969 cardigan and glasses)
positions.where: holding a FACS muscle-anatomy chart beside the screen logging Action Units AU1+4 before AU12 snaps on at Frame 17

props.name: 16mm flatbed Steenbeck film viewer
props.period_detail: brushed-aluminum editing table displaying crisp sequential portrait frames on its frosted screen
props.physical_behavior: freezes the 83-millisecond brow flash invisible at 24 fps

props.name: three-frame contact strip ('Frame 13 Neutral / Frame 14-15 Distress / Frame 17 Polite Smile')
props.period_detail: enlarged black-and-white photographic strip resting on the desk

props.name: anatomical Facial Action Coding chart
props.period_detail: clean medical line drawing mapping numbered forehead and cheek muscles (AU1, AU4, AU6, AU12)

actions.verb_sequence: plays the 16mm interview at full speed showing an unbroken polite smile -> rewinds -> clicks the hand wheel two single frames forward exposing the hidden distress brow
matches the brow angle to Action Units 1+4 on the anatomical chart

reactions.reaction: circles 'Frame 14-15 (0.08 sec)' on the strip in astonishment
writes 'Concealed Distress — Check Context (Avoid Othello's Error)' in the margin

scenes.wardrobe: 1969 San Francisco academic wear: Ekman in tweed jacket over collared shirt; Friesen in wool button cardigan and tie.
scenes.lighting: High-key daylight laboratory room balancing crisp bright Steenbeck viewer glass.
scenes.recognition_hook: Invisible at full 24-frames-per-second speed, stepping the 16mm film two frames forward exposes an 83-millisecond flash of anguish before the polite smile locks shut.

key_visual.description: two 1969 psychologists at a 16mm flatbed film-editing console pointing at a frozen two-frame facial expression strip beside an anatomical muscle Action Unit chart

scenes.title: Eight years mapping 44 Facial Action Units in a mirror

layout.description: Bright studio desk with an angled mirror, anatomical skull-muscle drawings, and numbered AU reference cards.

positions.where: isolating single brow and cheek contractions in a desk mirror to verify Action Unit independence

props.name: 44 Action Unit reference binder
props.physical_behavior: replaces vague adjectives with exact muscle mechanics

actions.verb_sequence: isolates AU6 cheek-raiser + AU12 lip-puller vs AU12 alone

scenes.recognition_hook: Cataloging 44 exact muscle units turned fuzzy 'intuition' into repeatable science — and later Pixar animation.

scenes.title: Othello's Error: Innocent anxiety vs guilty anxiety look identical

layout.description: Split comparison of two identical interview tables where an honest nervous witness and a deceptive witness show the exact same tense brow.

positions.where: pausing judgment and checking verifiable timeline documents instead of guessing from nerves

props.name: objective timeline verification folder
props.period_detail: hard factual evidence vs 54% demeanor guessing

actions.verb_sequence: sets aside gut hunches -> asks calm open-ended timeline questions

scenes.recognition_hook: Fear on an innocent face looks identical to fear on a guilty face — never confuse emotion with a lie.

scenes.title: Using a fleeting expression as an empathy cue, not a gotcha

layout.description: Sunlit office lounge where one colleague notices a brief flash of concern when deadlines come up and gently asks 'Do we need more runway?'

positions.where: seated across a small round table in open supportive conversation

actions.verb_sequence: spots brief tension behind 'Sure, fine!' -> gently asks 'What part feels tight?' -> Colleague B opens up relieved

reactions.reaction: exhales gratefully and points out the bottleneck

scenes.recognition_hook: Used with humility, noticing a fleeting flash opens compassionate conversation instead of armchair policing.
